President Trump says there's an energy ceasefire
between Russia and Ukraine,
but Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky
says he doesn't have the details
and Russia hasn't commented.
Zelensky also says his military
is ready to stop attacking Russian oil refineries
if Moscow halts its own attacks
on Ukraine's energy facilities.
NPR's Joanna Kasisis reports.
Writing on social media, Zelensky said any de-escalation
of strikes must be part of an energy ceasefire
and backed by real security guarantees.
The real cause of this war in Europe
is Russia and Russia alone, he said.
Zelensky slammed Trump's decision on Friday
to lift sanctions on Russian diesel.
The Ukrainian leader says this move will only prolong the war
and kill more civilians in Ukraine.
On Saturday, Russian bombs killed at least 23 people,
including four children, in apartment buildings
in the southeastern city of Zaporizha.
Trump blames Zelensky for the war
and says Ukraine must hold elections for a new president.
Joanna Kasisis, NPR News Cave.
Hackers are ramping up attacks on critical systems
from the water sector to hospitals,
now with the help of AI,
a collective of cybersecurity companies.
They're calling on the government to take action.
NPR's Joanna McLaughlin reports.
- In July, Iranian hackers disrupted water systems
across the United States.
Meanwhile, the Government Accountability Office
recently revealed that many federal agencies
don't even know what operational technology,
the tools that monitor physical processes like water pumps,
is connected to their networks.
Companies in the Operational Technology
Cybersecurity Coalition are urging the government
to mandate basic cybersecurity standards
for federal civilian agencies
when it comes to these kinds of critical systems.
Tatiana Bolton is the coalition's executive director.
Right now, federal agencies are operating
with massive blind spots.
She says the government needs to designate
federal officials with accountability
and segment networks for security.
General McLaughlin, NPR News.
- New inflation numbers are due out this week.
NPR's Stephen Bichaha reports the data
will be closely watched by investors concerning interest rates.
- The Federal Reserve's Preferred Inflation Index
showed that inflation came in lower
than expected for August.
But Fed Chair Kevin Worsch has said
they don't rely on any one figure,
so if September's Consumer Price Index comes in hot,
that would add pressure for the Fed
to raise rates later this month.
The CPI comes out Wednesday.
Before that, on Tuesday, we'll get September's
existing home sales from the National Association of Realtors.
Sales cooled in August due to high mortgage rates.
Rates have only gone up sharply since then.
Last week, the average for the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage
was 7.4 percent.
Stephen Bichaha, NPR News, Birmingham, Alabama.
- It's NPR.
There's a new drug for patients with schizophrenia.
It's a monthly injection.
NPR's Sydney Lopkin reports.
- The Food and Drug Administration
has approved Welltrusa.
It contains a drug ingredient that's been used
for 30 years for patients with schizophrenia,
but instead of a daily pill, it's a monthly injection.
That could be a big help for patients
who have a hard time remembering to take a pill every day.
Missing doses could cause someone's schizophrenia symptoms,
like delusions or disorganized thinking, to return.
Instead, Welltrusa can keep concentrations
of the drug in the blood more even over time.
Teva Pharmaceuticals, which makes the drugs,
set the list price at around $4,000 per injection,
but that's the price before insurance.
It's unclear how widely the drug will be covered
or how much patients' copays will cost.
Sydney Lopkin, NPR News.
- AAA says the national average price
for both unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel
declined last week, but both remain higher
than they were a month ago.
Unleaded regular average is $4.35 a gallon nationally.
That's down a penny from yesterday.
Diesel dipped to $6.27 down one cent.
However, a month ago, gasoline was $4.29,
six cents less expensive.
Diesel was at $6.05, 22 cents less expensive.
The price of diesel has been closely watched
by trucking companies, the railroads,
and agricultural companies, as it's a key component,
in the price of transporting groceries
from the farm to market.
I'm Dan Ronan, NPR News, Washington.

Federal Reserve's preferred inflation index comes in lower than expected for August
